page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.m1 server family. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical cores, operating with a single thread per core. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The underlying virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, requiring reliance on network-attached storage options for operating system deployment and data persistence. The CPU configuration lacks advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, or specialized cryptographic hardware acceleration flags. This makes the instance less suitable for heavy vector math, machine learning inference, or intensive cryptographic processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance without the risk of resource contention common in shared-core environments. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes the ecs.m1.xlarge appropriate for general-purpose workloads, including medium-traffic web servers, application hosting, microservices, and development or testing environments that require stable, non-burstable CPU performance.
